briefing.headline: Nothing in the fifteen is injured and £0.1m in the bank blocks every upgrade worth having, so this is a week to fix the armband, tidy the XI and bank the transfer.

do.action: Move the vice-captaincy from Cherki to João Pedro.
do.why: João Pedro is on 5.88 xP next against Hull (H, FDR 2), Cherki on 4.26 and averaging 67 minutes a game. If Haaland is a late scratch at Old Trafford you want the higher-scoring, safest-minutes replacement, not a City player who may be rotated in the same fixture.

do.action: Bank the free transfer and go into GW5 with two.
do.why: The only genuinely dead asset is Kusi-Asare (0.41 xP next, 2.3 over five, 15% chance of playing, 49 career minutes) and with £0.1m in the bank he sells for £4.5m into a £4.6m budget — no forward in the data is available at that price. Everything else in the XI is playing 77-90 minutes with no flags. A marginal sideways move now costs you the flexibility to make a funded double move next week.

consider.why: For: +3.3 xP over five (25.3 v 22.0), it frees £2.4m which turns Kusi-Asare into a playing forward next week (Calvert-Lewin 21.0, Awoniyi 21.2 both come into range), and it opens a Man City slot you currently have filled to the 3-player limit. Against: 3.3 points over five gameweeks is inside model noise, Tavernier is owned by 1.0% of the top 10k so you carry the whole downside alone, and you are selling an £8.4m attacker on a run of MUN(a), SUN(h), LIV(a) that could turn on one goal. At a 3.3m rank the differential is defensible; if you prefer to keep the ceiling, hold.

For: 4.02 v 3.86 next week, and Coventry are at home to Brighton (FDR 2) while Everton go to Spurs (FDR 3). Against: the gap is 0.16 points — a coin flip — van Ewijk's rating rests on 270 minutes all from this season, and Tarkowski is ahead over five (19.8 v 16.8). Either is fine; if you want the safer floor, leave the XI as it is.

ignore.action: Chasing Isak because 68.3% of the top 10k own him.
ignore.why: He is £9.1m against £0.1m in the bank, so it is not a one-transfer move at all. The model also has him at 18.0 over five on thin evidence — 937 minutes of it, only 243 this season — and 72 minutes a game. It is a real rank exposure, but not one you can fix this week.

ignore.action: Buying Palmer (6.23 xP) or B.Fernandes (5.94 xP) because they top the next-gameweek list.
ignore.why: £9.6m and £12.0m respectively; your maximum spend on a midfielder is £8.5m. They are noise on this deadline.

ignore.action: Upgrading a defender to Guéhi (23.3 over five) or Gvardiol.
ignore.why: You already hold Haaland, Cherki and Semenyo — three Man City players. The squad rule blocks it until one of them leaves.

ignore.action: Playing the Wildcard because the overall rank is 3.3m.
ignore.why: A bad rank is not a trigger. There are no injuries or flags in the fifteen and only one dead slot. Hold it for a fixture swing or a genuine pile-up of problems, but remember the first set expires at the GW19 deadline.
Your bench is Kinsky 2.61, Maguire 3.22, Tarkowski 3.86 and Kusi-Asare 0.41. That is roughly ten points for a chip that should be saved for a double gameweek with fifteen players actually starting.

captain.why: João Pedro is nominally ahead on next-gameweek xP (5.88 v 5.57) with the kinder fixture, but 93.3% of the sampled top 10k captain Haaland and 94.0% own him. Handing the armband elsewhere for 0.3 of an expected point is a pure variance play with no edge: if Haaland hauls at Old Trafford you lose two gameweeks of rank in one afternoon. Take the field's captain and win your rank back through the differentials in the rest of the XI.

briefing.chips: No chip this week. Triple Captain is gone from the first set, there is no blank or double in the next five gameweeks so Free Hit has no trigger, Bench Boost would be worth about ten points with Kusi-Asare on 0.41, and the Wildcard has no case with a fully fit fifteen. Keep all three, but note the Wildcard, Free Hit and Bench Boost in set one must be played by the GW19 deadline or they are lost.
risks: Predicted lineups were fetched on 10 September, two days before the deadline; Man City rotation in the derby would hit Haaland, Cherki and Semenyo at once, and your captaincy with them.
van Ewijk's 4.02 xP comes from 270 minutes, all this season — one dropped start and the bench decision looks silly.
Tavernier, if you take him, is a 1.0%-owned model pick; a 3.3-point projected edge over five weeks is well inside the model's error, and the model does not price set-piece duty at all.
Selling prices are assumed at current value; any move that leaves you at £0.0m could be £0.1m short in the app.
Banking the transfer is only right if nothing breaks between now and Saturday — check the 15 for late news before the 12:30 deadline.
